# Ezekiel 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-He-said to-me, "Son-of man, stand upon your-feet, and-I-will-speak with-you."

**2** And-the-spirit entered into-me when-He-spoke to-me, and-it-stood-me upon my-feet, and-I-heard [the one]-speaking to-me.

**3** And-He-said to-me, "Son-of man, I [am]-sending you to the-sons-of Israel, to nations rebellious who-have-rebelled against-Me — they and-their-fathers have-transgressed against-Me until this-very day.

**4** And-the-sons [are] hard-of face and-stiff-of heart — I [am]-sending you to-them, and-you-shall-say to-them, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH.'

**5** And-they — whether they-hear or-whether they-refuse, for a-house-of rebellion they [are] — they-will-know that a-prophet has-been in-their-midst.

**6** And-you, son-of man, do-not-be-afraid of-them and-of-their-words do-not-be-afraid, though briers and-thorns [are] with-you and-upon scorpions you sit; of-their-words do-not-be-afraid and-of-their-faces do-not-be-dismayed, for a-house-of rebellion they [are].

**7** And-you-shall-speak My-words to-them, whether they-hear or-whether they-refuse, for rebellious they [are].

**8** And-you, son-of man, hear what I [am]-speaking to-you — do-not-be rebellious like-the-house-of the-rebellion; open your-mouth and-eat what I [am]-giving to-you."

**9** And-I-looked, and-behold, a-hand [was] stretched-out to-me, and-behold, in-it [was] a-scroll-of a-book.

**10** And-He-spread-it before-me, and-it [was] written front and-back, and-written upon-it [were] lamentations and-mourning and-woe.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **2:1**: Ben-adam — 'son of man.' Used 93 times in Ezekiel, emphasizing the prophet's humanity in contrast to the divine glory. Not messianic here but a marker of mortal creatureliness.

- **2:9-10**: Megillat-sefer — 'scroll of a book.' Written front and back (unusual, indicating fullness of the message). The contents — qinot, hegeh, hi — lamentations, mourning, woe — summarize Ezekiel's entire prophetic burden.

- **2:6**: Sarabim ve-salonim — 'briers and thorns.' Metaphor for hostile reception. The scorpion imagery intensifies the danger. The fourfold 'do not fear' echoes prophetic call patterns.

— EMET
